acceptance_criteria.criterion: After any call to csRefreshWithStores(), at most one element with id cs-notification-banner exists in the DOM
The sync popover does not overflow the right viewport edge — when it would, its left is set to auto and right is set to 0
When the popover is hidden, inline left and right styles are cleared (reset to default positioning for next show)

summary: Added banner dedup guard in csRefreshWithStores(): after innerHTML assignment, querySelector('#cs-notification-banner') removes any existing banner before the new one is injected.
Added viewport overflow check in mouseenter and focus sync badge handlers: after classList.add, getBoundingClientRect().right > window.innerWidth triggers style.left='auto' and style.right='0'.
Added inline style reset in mouseleave and blur sync badge handlers: after classList.remove, style.left='' and style.right='' clear the flip positioning for the next show.

comments.note: The `rect` variable is re-declared in both mouseenter and focus handlers inside the same IIFE scope. These are separate event handler functions so there's no shadowing issue, but the naming is consistent. No issue here.

The overflow check uses getBoundingClientRect() which works correctly after classList.add makes the popover visible. However, the popover must be rendered in its default (left-aligned) position before the rect check, otherwise the right value may be incorrect on re-show after a right-aligned display. The reset in hide handlers (left='', right='') correctly ensures this.

summary: AC1: csRefreshWithStores() replaces innerHTML, removes any existing banner (querySelector + remove), then conditionally inserts one new banner — at most one banner in DOM.
AC2: mouseenter and focus handlers call classList.add first, then getBoundingClientRect() for accurate overflow measurement, then set left='auto', right='0' when rect.right > window.innerWidth.
AC3: mouseleave and blur handlers call classList.remove then unconditionally set style.left='' and style.right='' to reset for next show.

comments.note: The getBoundingClientRect() overflow check correctly fires after classList.add (popover visible), so the measured rect.right is accurate. The hide-handler style reset ensures the next show always starts from the default (left-aligned) position before the check runs. The pattern is self-consistent.

No automated tests cover csRefreshWithStores() banner dedup or the popover flip logic (frontend-only JS). JSDOM-based tests would require mocking getBoundingClientRect() and window.innerWidth, which is achievable if needed in future.

summary: All three acceptance criteria verified by code inspection.

Banner dedup guard: render (innerHTML) → remove old banner (querySelector + remove) → optionally inject new banner — correct pattern ensuring at most one banner in DOM regardless of what renderStoresTab() includes.

Popover overflow: classList.add → getBoundingClientRect() → conditional flip — correct ordering ensures measurement is taken from visible popover. Style reset on hide is unconditional, making the hide path idempotent across viewport-width changes.

comments.note: The classList.add → getBoundingClientRect() → style-flip ordering is the correct sequence for accurate popover overflow detection. Measuring before classList.add would give dimensions of the hidden element (display:none or visibility:hidden depending on CSS), producing an incorrect (likely 0) rect.right. The current ordering ensures the measurement is always taken from the visible popover.

The unconditional style reset in hide handlers (style.left='' and style.right='') is the right choice even when the flip was not applied. It makes the hide path idempotent and eliminates an edge case where a previously flipped popover could retain its right-aligned positioning on subsequent shows in a wider viewport.

[documentation-forward] The four sync badge event handlers (mouseenter/mouseleave/focus/blur) within each IIFE contain duplicated popover-lookup-and-act logic. When this module is eventually modernised, factoring these into showSyncPopover(popover) and hideSyncPopover(popover) helper functions would reduce duplication significantly. Low priority — acceptable in current ES5 style.
